A.notes:
the All sections page looks good. 

I am not convinced that the accordions on the activity charts page are the best solution, but they are a reasonable solution and much better than displaying all of that content at once. 

The Activity charts page does not use the filter bar and still has a 'sort' button to apply a selection. Also the checkbox to 'reverse order' is not vertically aligned with it surrounding content.

B.notes:
On the all section page, the content under 'about these figures' does not justify an accordion. It is too short. That reads more like it should be a footnote below the cards. 

The sidebar on the activity charts page does not work. The round 6 agents were right that it makes the visualizations content too narrow, and the sidebar is nearly empty when the accordion is closed.

C.notes:
Like with Build b, the accordion on the all sections page is not justified because the text is very short. It is more like a footnote. 

The filterbar on the activity charts page looks good. 

The sidebar is not the right choice because it reduces the space for the visualizations which are the primary content. Perhaps a tooltip or button that opens a modal is the right solution. Interesting that no agent tried that. Do we have any insight into wether it was considered and rejected? To be honest, as a human I would need to test out each of our relevant affordances to see which one works best. Maybe we should ask agents to think in that way too?

A note for all of the builds at phone width: the secondary navigation wraps to two lines and is hard to read. We should explore options for a condensed secondary nav. Throwing out some ideas: a hamburder menu, some other menu icon, only displaying the first tab label with icons or initial letter  or numbers on the other tabs, a mini carousel/slider with the current label in the center and back and next arrows. These ideas are just to get the brainstorming going. This can be rolled into a larger discussion of compact elements.

D.notes:
On the activity charts page, interesting use of a sidebar for t he list of categories. I think this will not work in real life though because this page will list many, many visualizations in the main column, and that will leave wasted space on the right side where the sidebar column is empty. Also on that page, this build did not use the filter bar. 

A note for all builds: put a card border around the placeholder content, it will make it easier to "read" the page.

together:
A sidebar was used in 3 of 4 and was the reason I rejected those builds. It really is not a good use of space. The previous build agents were right about that. 

No builds tried a tooltip or a modal for revealing extra content. And no builds displayed long about content on the page at the bottom. Interesting. Why do you think that is?
